Feast-day recipes

Zopf

Served at: Berchtoldstag

Serves 8-10Prep 30 min active + 2-3 hours risingCook 35-40 min

Zopf, meaning "braid" in Swiss German, is a rich, buttery braided bread that is a beloved staple in Switzerland. Traditionally enjoyed on Sunday mornings, it also holds a special place during holidays like Berchtoldstag, the New Year's Day celebration in many Swiss cantons. Its golden crust and tender crumb make it a comforting and festive start to the new year, often served with butter and jam.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, warmed to 105-115°F (40-46°C)
  • 2 ¼ teaspoons (7g) active dry yeast (one standard packet)
  • 1 teaspoon granulated sugar
  • 4 ½ cups (540g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 ½ teaspoons (9g) fine sea salt
  • ½ cup (113g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • 1 large egg, plus 1 egg yolk (for the dough)
  • 1 large egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine the warm milk, yeast, and 1 teaspoon of sugar. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour and salt.
  3. Add the melted butter, 1 large egg, and 1 egg yolk to the yeast mixture, and whisk to combine.
  4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix with a wooden spoon or stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
  5. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, or use a stand mixer on medium-low speed for 6-8 minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
  6. Lightly grease a clean bowl with oil, place the dough in it, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  7. Punch down the risen dough gently and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Divide the dough into two equal pieces.
  8. Roll each piece into a long strand, about 18-20 inches (45-50 cm) long, tapering slightly at the ends.
  9. Place the two strands parallel to each other. Cross the right strand over the left. Then take the new right strand and cross it over the left. Continue this simple over-under pattern, always taking the strand that is now on the right and crossing it over the left, until you reach the end. Pinch the ends together to seal.
  10. Carefully transfer the braided loaf to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let it rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
  11. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C) during the second rise.
  12. Brush the top and sides of the risen Zopf generously with the beaten egg wash.
  13. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 200-210°F (93-99°C). If it browns too quickly, you can loosely tent it with foil.
  14. Transfer the Zopf to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For an extra shiny crust, brush with egg wash again halfway through baking.
  • Ensure your milk is not too hot, as it can kill the yeast. It should feel comfortably warm to the touch.
  • Zopf is best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be lightly toasted or used for French toast.
